citations.title: APIRef_tm_sys_file_ssl-cert
citations.supports: Module: F5 BIG-IP certificate install via iControl REST
citations.key_fact: The /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert collection supports GET; individual certificate resources support GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, are keyed by name, partition and subPath, and take an optional sourcePath property that names the URI the certificate file is copied from.

citations.title: sslcertkey | configuration
citations.supports: Module: NetScaler certificate install via NITRO API
citations.key_fact: Creating a certificate-key pair is a POST to /nitro/v1/config/sslcertkey with a JSON body whose mandatory fields are certkey and cert (paths point to files on the appliance disk, typically /nsconfig/ssl); a successful add returns 201, and UPDATE is a PUT to the same URL with certkey mandatory and optional fields such as expirymonitor and notificationperiod.

citations.title: Create a certificate signing request and use SSL certificates on a NetScaler appliance | How-to articles | NetScaler
citations.supports: Module: NetScaler certificate binding to SSL vservers
citations.key_fact: After installing the cert and key under /nsconfig/ssl you run add ssl certKey <name> -cert <file> -key <file> (optionally -expiryMonitor ENABLED -notificationPeriod <days>), link any intermediate certificates first, then bind with bind ssl vserver <vs> -certkeyName <name> and verify with show ssl vserver; every SSL virtual server needs its own valid binding.

citations.title: Install an SSL Certificate on a Radware Alteon Application Switch
citations.supports: Module: Radware Alteon certificate management
citations.key_fact: On Alteon the installation flow is to build one PEM file with the server certificate followed by the intermediate chain, enter the cfg then cert menu on the switch CLI, paste the PEM, terminate the input with three periods, and then run apply to activate the change (no official Radware public page could be fetched, so this CA guide is the best available source).

citations.title: RFC 8555: Automatic Certificate Management Environment (ACME)
citations.supports: Module: ACME and internal CA renewal workflow
citations.key_fact: ACME replaces manual Web PKI steps with machine-readable exchanges: a client creates an account, submits an order for identifiers, satisfies one of the challenges offered in each authorization to prove control, finalizes the order with a CSR and then downloads the issued certificate; the protocol also covers revocation.

citations.title: openssl-verify - OpenSSL Documentation
citations.supports: Module: OpenSSL verification of installed chains
citations.key_fact: openssl verify validates certificate chains and tries to report every problem it finds rather than stopping at the first; -CAfile supplies trusted anchors while -untrusted (repeatable) supplies intermediates used only for chain building, not as trust anchors.

citations.title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
citations.supports: Module: building an MCP server for load balancer APIs
citations.key_fact: MCP is an open-source standard, likened to a USB-C port for AI applications, that lets AI apps connect to data sources, tools and workflows in a uniform way; it is supported by Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor and others so a server built once works across clients.

citations.title: Overview - Claude Code
citations.supports: Module: orchestrating renewals with Claude Code
citations.key_fact: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool available in terminal, IDE, desktop app and browser; it can be scripted non-interactively with claude -p for piping and CI use, connects to external systems through MCP, supports hooks that run shell commands before or after its actions, and can run cloud or desktop scheduled tasks for recurring work.

citations.title: Agent SDK overview
citations.supports: Module: building a renewal agent with the Claude Agent SDK
citations.key_fact: The Agent SDK exposes the same tools, agent loop and context management as Claude Code as a Python or TypeScript library, with built-in tools, hooks, subagents, MCP connections, permission controls, resumable sessions, skills and plugins; third-party products must use API-key authentication rather than claude.ai logins.

citations.title: Installing BIG-IP Version 17.5.1.4
citations.supports: Module: F5 BIG-IP software image install (tmsh install sys software image)
citations.key_fact: The ISO must be placed in /shared/images and installed to an inactive volume with `tmsh install sys software image <iso> volume HD1.x`; progress is watched with `tmsh show sys software` and logged to /var/log/liveinstall.log. A UCS backup must be saved first, mirroring turned off, and on redundant pairs the standby unit is upgraded and verified before the active unit.

citations.title: Upgrading Version 11.x or 12.x BIG-IP Software
citations.supports: Module: F5 BIG-IP HA / device group upgrade sequence and pre-checks
citations.key_fact: Each device in a device group is forced offline (moving its traffic groups to a peer) before it is upgraded, one device at a time; mirroring does not function until every device has rebooted onto the new version, so F5 tells you to do this inside a maintenance window. Preparation includes config sync, RAID health check, QKView to iHealth, UCS backup, and image checksum verification.

citations.title: Upgrade a high availability pair
citations.supports: Module: Citrix NetScaler HA pair upgrade order
citations.key_fact: Upgrade the secondary node first, force a failover so it becomes primary, then upgrade the former primary. While the two nodes run builds with different internal HA versions, config sync, command propagation, connection mirroring, and persistence-session sync are disabled; `show ha node` should be run beforehand to confirm the node state.

citations.title: Before you begin | Upgrade and downgrade a NetScaler appliance
citations.supports: Module: NetScaler disk space and pre-upgrade validation checks
citations.key_fact: NetScaler 14.1 requires at least 7 GB free in /var (1 GB bundle, 2 GB extraction, 4 GB upgrade process) and at least 250 MB free in /flash. The page also says to upgrade one major release at a time, allocate roughly twice the normal time, back up config/certs/licenses, remove /var/customizations, run the preconfiguration check tool, run fsck on hardware, and test in non-production first.

citations.title: Upgrade Path (AlteonOS 33.5.2.0 Release Notes)
citations.supports: Module: Radware Alteon software upgrade path, pre-upgrade steps and rollback
citations.key_fact: Before upgrading, back up the configuration and run the Upgrade Advisor Tool (from the Radware Customer Portal, with its database updated) against the current config and target version. Versions 31.x-33.x upgrade directly, older ones need intermediate hops; configuration rollback is not supported, so downgrading means booting the old image with factory config and re-uploading the saved configuration.

citations.title: Updating Device Software
citations.supports: Module: Radware device software update workflow (File > Software Update)
citations.key_fact: Radware's device update flow requires an upgrade password obtained from Radware support that is tied to the device's base MAC address and the software file size; after backing up the configuration, the operator enters the version and file, chooses whether to enable the new version immediately, applies the update, and the device reboots and must be verified on the console.

citations.title: Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning: Preventive Maintenance for Technology (NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4)
citations.supports: Module: scheduling and framing upgrades as routine preventive maintenance
citations.key_fact: Published April 2022, SP 800-40r4 defines enterprise patch management as identifying, prioritizing, acquiring, installing, and verifying patches, updates, and upgrades, and frames it as preventive maintenance that organizations should operationalize with an enterprise-wide strategy rather than treat as ad hoc work.

Confirms back up configuration before upgrade, run the Upgrade Advisor Tool on the Customer Portal and update its DB first, direct upgrade from 31.x/32.x/33.x, intermediate hops for older versions (e.g. 28.x -> 29.0.9.0 -> 30.5.3.0 -> this version), 'Configuration rollback (downgrade) is not supported', and downgrade by booting the older image with factory-default config then uploading the previously saved configuration. Note: the page's upgrade-path table references 33.5.1.0 as target while the title says 33.5.2.0 (doc inconsistency on Radware's side).

citations.supports: Module 2: LinkedIn Talent API integration options for an ATS
citations.key_fact: LinkedIn Talent Solutions offers partner-facing APIs grouped as Apply Connect, Apply with LinkedIn, Job Posting API, CRM Connect and Recruiter System Connect; Recruiter System Connect synchronises candidate information between an ATS and LinkedIn Recruiter, while the Job Posting API ingests jobs already created in an ATS or job board.

citations.key_fact: Naukri has no self-serve developer portal: an employer must request its team's API key from its Naukri point of contact, Naukri requires a paid subscription to post jobs (which may cap active postings), and postings fail unless location, experience range and job role are present and correctly formatted.

citations.title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (No. 22 of 2023) - Gazette of India Extraordinary
citations.publisher: Government of India (Gazette copy hosted by TRAI)
citations.supports: Module 5: lawful basis, notice and consent for candidate data under DPDP Act 2023
citations.key_fact: Section 5 requires every consent request to be accompanied or preceded by a notice stating the personal data and purpose, how to exercise rights and how to complain to the Board; Section 6 requires consent to be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action; and Section 7(i) lists processing for the purposes of employment as a 'certain legitimate use' that does not require consent.

citations.title: DPDP Rules, 2025 Notified - A Citizen-Centric Framework for Privacy Protection and Responsible Data Use

citations.title: CEFR - Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
citations.publisher: lifelong-learning.lu (INFPC, Government of Luxembourg lifelong-learning portal)
citations.supports: Module 3: scoring candidate English proficiency on the CEFR scale
citations.key_fact: CEFR has six levels grouped into three bands: Basic user (A1 Breakthrough, A2 Waystage), Independent user (B1 Threshold, B2 Vantage) and Proficient user (C1 Effective operational proficiency, C2 Mastery); B2 is where a candidate can follow complex technical text in their field and converse fluently with native speakers, and levels can be subdivided locally (for example A1.1/A1.2).

citations.key_fact: GST law prescribes no fixed invoice layout, but Rule 46 of the CGST Rules 2017 makes a set of fields mandatory; a registered person making taxable supplies issues a tax invoice, while composition dealers or exempt-only suppliers issue a bill of supply, and no invoice is needed for supplies under Rs. 200 subject to conditions.

citations.title: RFC 1393: Traceroute Using an IP Option
citations.supports: Module 1: traceroute fundamentals and the IP Traceroute option
citations.key_fact: Classic TTL-based traceroute needs roughly 2n packets for n hops; RFC 1393 proposed an IP Traceroute option plus an ICMP Traceroute message (type 30) so each router reports back directly, cutting this to about n+1 packets and avoiding mid-trace path shifts. It is Experimental and was later obsoleted by RFC 6814.

citations.title: RFC 792: Internet Control Message Protocol
citations.supports: Module 1: ping fundamentals (ICMP Echo/Echo Reply) and Time Exceeded
citations.key_fact: ICMP Echo is type 8 and Echo Reply is type 0, with identifier and sequence fields used to match replies to requests and the received data echoed back unchanged; Time Exceeded is type 11, with code 0 meaning TTL exceeded in transit, which is the message traceroute relies on.

citations.title: Use the Traceroute Command on Operating Systems - Cisco
citations.supports: Module 1: how traceroute probes work on Cisco IOS, Linux and Windows
citations.key_fact: Cisco IOS and Linux traceroute send UDP probes starting at destination port 33434 with TTL starting at 1 (default max 30 hops); each hop returns ICMP Time Exceeded (type 11, code 0) and the destination returns ICMP Port Unreachable (type 3, code 3). Windows tracert uses ICMP Echo instead, and Cisco routers rate-limit ICMP unreachables (default one per 500 ms), which can show up as missing hops.

citations.title: GitHub - traviscross/mtr: Official repository for mtr, a network diagnostic tool
citations.supports: Module 2: continuous path measurement with mtr
citations.key_fact: mtr combines traceroute and ping in one tool: it sends probes with successively larger TTL values to discover the path and then prints running per-hop statistics. The README warns that routers may not respond to or may rate-limit ICMP, so apparent loss at an intermediate hop does not necessarily mean forwarded traffic is being dropped there.

citations.title: Flowcharts Syntax | Mermaid
citations.supports: Module 3: Mermaid flowchart syntax for network path diagrams
citations.key_fact: Flowcharts start with `flowchart` (or `graph`) plus a direction keyword (TB/TD, BT, RL, LR); edges include `-->`, `---`, dotted `-.-`, thick `===`, and `--o`/`--x`; `subgraph id [Title] ... end` groups nodes and can carry its own direction; from v11.3.0 shapes can be set with `A@{ shape: ... }`. A lowercase `end` inside a node label breaks the diagram.

citations.title: What Is AWS Config?
citations.supports: Module: cloud inventory APIs (AWS Config)
citations.key_fact: AWS Config records the configuration and inter-resource relationships of AWS resources over time, and an aggregator can pull configuration and compliance data from many accounts and Regions into one place for a centralized inventory view.

citations.title: Overview of Azure Resource Graph - Azure Resource Graph | Microsoft Learn
citations.supports: Module: cloud inventory APIs (Azure Resource Graph)
citations.key_fact: Azure Resource Graph lets you query resource properties at scale across subscriptions using a KQL-based language, returns only resources you have at least read RBAC access to, and keeps 14 days of resource configuration change history; its data is eventually consistent rather than strongly consistent.

citations.title: Certificate Transparency
citations.supports: Module: Certificate Transparency logs as an asset-discovery source
citations.key_fact: CT logs are publicly auditable, append-only, untrusted logs of issued certificates, designed so anyone can monitor CA activity and detect suspicious or unexpected certificates.

citations.title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
citations.supports: Module: building a CT log monitor for new subdomains/certificates
citations.key_fact: RFC 9162 defines the monitor role and requires that a monitor inspect at least every new entry in every log it watches, which is the same pattern an attack surface tool uses when watching CT logs for newly issued certificates on an organization's domains.

citations.title: crt.sh | Certificate Search
citations.supports: Module: hands-on subdomain discovery via crt.sh
citations.key_fact: crt.sh is a search front end over Certificate Transparency data that lets you look up certificates by identity (domain or organization name), by SHA-1/SHA-256 fingerprint, or by crt.sh ID, with an advanced search mode available.

citations.title: Domain Names - Concepts and Facilities
citations.supports: Module: DNS fundamentals and passive DNS
citations.key_fact: DNS data is organized into zones, each authoritative for a connected region of the name space; each node holds a set of resource records whose order carries no meaning, and name servers may also cache non-authoritative data for other parts of the tree.

citations.title: Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment (NIST SP 800-115)
citations.supports: Module: authorized scope and rules of engagement
citations.key_fact: NIST defines Rules of Engagement as detailed guidelines and constraints for executing security testing, established before testing starts so the team has authority to perform defined activities without needing further permission; Appendix B supplies an ROE template.

citations.title: Configuration Management Database (CMDB)
citations.supports: Module: CMDB concepts and entity resolution against the inventory
citations.key_fact: A CMDB stores assets, services and the relationships between them as configuration items (CIs), which teams rely on to monitor infrastructure and keep it stable; external discovery results must be reconciled against these CIs.

citations.title: WSTG - v4.2 | OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (4.1 Information Gathering)
citations.supports: Module: reconnaissance and application enumeration on discovered assets
citations.key_fact: WSTG section 4.1 lists ten information gathering tests, including search engine reconnaissance for information leakage, fingerprinting the web server, enumerating applications on a web server, identifying application entry points and mapping application architecture.

Page confirms query at scale across subscriptions, KQL-based query language, 'View the last 14 days of resource configuration changes', at least 'read' RBAC access required or no results returned, and 'Azure Resource Graph data isn't strongly consistent' (eventual consistency).

citations.title: JSON output format | Terraform | HashiCorp Developer
citations.supports: Module 2: parsing Terraform plan JSON for review
citations.key_fact: The plan JSON from `terraform show -json` carries a format_version ("1.0" since Terraform 1.1.0) and a resource_changes array whose change.actions values are no-op, create, read, update, delete, or the two replacement orderings ["delete","create"] / ["create","delete"], so a reviewer can detect any destructive change by checking for "delete".

citations.title: Pod Security Standards | Kubernetes
citations.supports: Module 3: Kubernetes YAML hardening checks against Pod Security Standards
citations.key_fact: The Restricted profile builds on Baseline and requires allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, runAsNonRoot: true, a non-zero runAsUser, seccompProfile.type of RuntimeDefault or Localhost, capabilities.drop containing ALL with only NET_BIND_SERVICE allowed to be added, and restricts volumes to types such as configMap, secret, emptyDir, projected, csi, ephemeral and persistentVolumeClaim.

citations.title: Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container | Kubernetes
citations.supports: Module 3: reading securityContext fields in Pod manifests
citations.key_fact: A pod-level securityContext (runAsUser, runAsGroup, fsGroup, supplementalGroups) applies to every container in the Pod, while container-level fields such as allowPrivilegeEscalation apply only to that container; allowPrivilegeEscalation defaults to true when unset and cannot be false for privileged or CAP_SYS_ADMIN containers.

citations.title: Terraform | Open Policy Agent
citations.supports: Module 4: policy-as-code evaluation of Terraform plans with OPA/Rego
citations.key_fact: OPA consumes the output of `terraform show -json` as `input`, and the tutorial policy walks resource_changes[].type and change.actions to compute a weighted blast-radius score, authorizing the plan only if the score is below 30 and no aws_iam resources change.

citations.title: Conftest
citations.supports: Module 4: running Rego policies against Kubernetes/Terraform config files with Conftest
citations.key_fact: Conftest evaluates Rego rules named deny, violation, and warn (optionally suffixed like deny_myrule) in the main namespace by default, against many structured formats including YAML, JSON, HCL/HCL2, Dockerfile, TOML, INI and XML.

citations.title: Misconfiguration Scanning - Trivy
citations.supports: Module 4: scanner-based misconfiguration checks with Trivy
citations.key_fact: `trivy config <dir>` auto-detects Terraform, Kubernetes, Dockerfile, CloudFormation, Azure ARM and Helm files and reports pass/fail counts per file by severity; with `trivy image` or `trivy fs` the misconfiguration scanner must be enabled explicitly via `--scanners misconfig`, and the checks bundle is downloaded from the internet unless an offline setup is used.

citations.title: What is Checkov? - checkov
citations.supports: Module 4: static IaC analysis with Checkov
citations.key_fact: Checkov statically analyzes Terraform, CloudFormation/SAM, ARM, Serverless, Helm, Kubernetes and Docker files with more than 750 predefined policies, supports custom policies, and maps results to benchmarks such as CIS and the AWS Foundations Benchmark.

citations.title: REST API endpoints for pull request review comments - GitHub Docs
citations.supports: Module 5: posting inline review findings via the GitHub pull request review comments API
citations.key_fact: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments` requires body, commit_id, path and line (line is optional only when subject_type is file); `position` is being phased out in favor of line, multi-line comments use start_line/start_side, and the endpoint can trigger secondary rate limits when called rapidly.

citations.title: REST API endpoints for check runs - GitHub Docs

citations.title: Threats - Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool - Azure | Microsoft Learn

citations.title: Threat Modeling - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series

citations.title: Threat Modeling Manifesto
citations.supports: Module 2: values and principles for agentic reviews
citations.key_fact: The Manifesto defines threat modeling as analyzing representations of a system to highlight security and privacy concerns, and values finding and fixing design issues over checkbox compliance, people and collaboration over process and tools, and continuous refinement over a single delivery.
